english.title: Promote an unlicensed lottery - Gambling Act 2005
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) promoted a lottery other than an exempt lottery

(A)_[without holding an operating licence authorising the activity]_
(B)_[while not acting in accordance with the terms and conditions of an operating licence]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 258(1) and 263(1) of the Gambling Act 2005.

english.notes:
(1) Section 258(3) of the Gambling Act 2005 provides that the offence does not apply to the activity by a person if
(a) he acts, otherwise than as an external lottery manager, on behalf of a person who holds an operating licence authorising the activity, and
(b) the activity is carried on in accordance with the terms and conditions of the licence.
(2) Section 258(4) of the Gambling Act 2005 provides that it is a defence for a person charged with this offence to show that he reasonably believed that-
(a) he was not committing the offence by reason of subsection (1)(b), (2) or (3),
(b) that the arrangement to which the charge relates was not a lottery, or
(c) that the arrangement to which the charge relates was a lottery forming part of the National Lottery.
(3) Section 258(5) of the Gambling Act 2005 provides that "exempt lottery" means a lottery which is exempt by virtue of a provision of Schedule 11 to the Gambling Act 2005.
(4) For the territorial application of this offence see section 265 of the Gambling Act 2005. That section also includes a defence, where a person reasonably believed that the lottery was outside the territorial application of this offence.
(5) A licensing authority may institute criminal proceedings in respect of this offence, section 346(1) of the Gambling Act 2005.

other.penalty:
Fifty one weeks imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
12 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
